"title": "Spontaneous crystal fluctuation in hydrocarbon polymer-coated monolayer MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , WS 2 , and WSe 2 with strong photoluminescence enhancement",
"authors": "Takahiro Nakahara; Takashi Kobayashi; Tetsuji Dohi; Takeshi Yoshimura; Norifumi Fujimura; Daisuke Kiriya",
"field_subfield": "2D materials / optoelectronics (photoluminescence enhancement in monolayer TMDCs)",
"type_of_paper": "Experimental study (materials science / nanophotonics)",
"executive_summary": "Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) of the form MX 2 (M = Mo, W and X = S, Se) are attractive because of their three-atom-thick crystal structure and excellent mechanical robustness, and they show a direct band gap at the K and Kʹ points of the Brillouin zone, which makes them promising for optical transistors, light-emitting diodes, and solar cells. However, a major drawback is their poor photoluminescence (PL) intensity, which is caused by factors such as over-carrier concentrations, strains, and defects in the crystalline lattice. For the n-type sulfur-based compounds MoS 2 and WS 2 , p-type doping with chemicals such as 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (F4TCNQ) and tetrafluoro-1,4-benzoquinone enhances PL by reducing trion formation, and superacid treatment with bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) can produce PL enhancement of hundreds of times. These chemical methods are not effective for the selenium-based TMDCs MoSe 2 and WSe 2 , where oleic acid and hydrohalic acid treatments and defect repairing have been tried, and WSe 2 has been addressed by floating or inserting ions to remove the substrate effect. The authors note that there are different strategies for different TMDCs and that no universal strategy has been found. This paper introduces a universal postpreparation method that removes the substrate effect by a spontaneous fluctuation of monolayer TMDCs induced by coating with a simple hydrocarbon, paraffin. Because of the large thermal expansion coefficient of paraffin, the stain is effectively applied to the TMDCs during the coating process, and the paraffin-coated monolayers show spontaneous fluctuation that in an extreme case forms the shape of a bundle. During this fluctuation and deformation, the substrate effect is removed, and PL intensity improves remarkably in both sulfur- and selenium-based compounds. The paraffin used has a melting point of 42-45 °C, and the coating was performed by melting paraffin on a hot plate at 80 °C and dropping it onto a sample on a spin coater while applying a heat blower to keep the paraffin molten. The enhancement factors were 215-fold for MoS 2 , 55-fold for WS 2 , 9-fold for WSe 2 , and 50-fold for MoSe 2 , relative to the as-exfoliated flakes. For monolayer WS 2 , PL enhancement of about 36 times was observed through paraffin coating, and the normalized PL spectrum showed a decrease in the shoulder at the low-energy side, suggesting a decrease in the ratio of trion-derived PL signal. The mechanism is attributed to a combination of strain induced by the volume change caused by the high thermal expansion coefficient of the paraffin and the subsequent desorption of the monolayer flakes from the substrate, which occurs spontaneously. The authors conclude that this engineering method of hydrocarbon-coating is useful for straining thin 2D materials and is applicable for generating transparent and flexible optoelectronic devices in two-dimensional semiconductor materials, taking advantage of the transparency, flexibility, and biocompatibility of the paraffin.",

summary.title: Spontaneous crystal fluctuation in hydrocarbon polymer-coated monolayer MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , WS 2 , and WSe 2 with strong photoluminescence enhancement
summary.authors: Takahiro Nakahara; Takashi Kobayashi; Tetsuji Dohi; Takeshi Yoshimura; Norifumi Fujimura; Daisuke Kiriya
summary.field_subfield: 2D materials / optoelectronics (photoluminescence enhancement in monolayer TMDCs)
summary.executive_summary: Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) of the form MX 2 (M = Mo, W and X = S, Se) are attractive because of their three-atom-thick crystal structure and excellent mechanical robustness, and they show a direct band gap at the K and Kʹ points of the Brillouin zone, which makes them promising for optical transistors, light-emitting diodes, and solar cells. However, a major drawback is their poor photoluminescence (PL) intensity, which is caused by factors such as over-carrier concentrations, strains, and defects in the crystalline lattice. For the n-type sulfur-based compounds MoS 2 and WS 2 , p-type doping with chemicals such as 2,3,5,6-tetrafluoro-7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (F4TCNQ) and tetrafluoro-1,4-benzoquinone enhances PL by reducing trion formation, and superacid treatment with bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) can produce PL enhancement of hundreds of times. These chemical methods are not effective for the selenium-based TMDCs MoSe 2 and WSe 2 , where oleic acid and hydrohalic acid treatments and defect repairing have been tried, and WSe 2 has been addressed by floating or inserting ions to remove the substrate effect. The authors note that there are different strategies for different TMDCs and that no universal strategy has been found. This paper introduces a universal postpreparation method that removes the substrate effect by a spontaneous fluctuation of monolayer TMDCs induced by coating with a simple hydrocarbon, paraffin. Because of the large thermal expansion coefficient of paraffin, the stain is effectively applied to the TMDCs during the coating process, and the paraffin-coated monolayers show spontaneous fluctuation that in an extreme case forms the shape of a bundle. During this fluctuation and deformation, the substrate effect is removed, and PL intensity improves remarkably in both sulfur- and selenium-based compounds. The paraffin used has a melting point of 42-45 °C, and the coating was performed by melting paraffin on a hot plate at 80 °C and dropping it onto a sample on a spin coater while applying a heat blower to keep the paraffin molten. The enhancement factors were 215-fold for MoS 2 , 55-fold for WS 2 , 9-fold for WSe 2 , and 50-fold for MoSe 2 , relative to the as-exfoliated flakes. For monolayer WS 2 , PL enhancement of about 36 times was observed through paraffin coating, and the normalized PL spectrum showed a decrease in the shoulder at the low-energy side, suggesting a decrease in the ratio of trion-derived PL signal. The mechanism is attributed to a combination of strain induced by the volume change caused by the high thermal expansion coefficient of the paraffin and the subsequent desorption of the monolayer flakes from the substrate, which occurs spontaneously. The authors conclude that this engineering method of hydrocarbon-coating is useful for straining thin 2D materials and is applicable for generating transparent and flexible optoelectronic devices in two-dimensional semiconductor materials, taking advantage of the transparency, flexibility, and biocompatibility of the paraffin.

claims.description: Paraffin coating provides a universal strategy for enhancing PL in both sulfur- and selenium-based TMDCs.
The mechanism of PL enhancement is a combination of strain and desorption of the monolayer from the substrate.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether a single method can enhance PL in both sulfur- and selenium-based TMDCs. The authors hypothesize that removing the substrate effect universally improves PL in all TMDCs. The hypothesis is that coating with a simple hydrocarbon, paraffin, induces this spontaneous fluctuation. The predicted outcome is that paraffin's large thermal expansion coefficient effectively applies strain to the TMDCs. The predicted result is that the stain is effectively applied to the TMDCs during the coating process. The authors predict that PL intensity will improve remarkably in both sulfur- and selenium-based compounds. Methodological Details
The study used monolayer TMDCs of the form MX 2 with M = Mo, W and X = S, Se. The four compounds studied were MoS 2 , WS 2 , MoSe 2 , and WSe 2 . The samples were prepared as as-exfoliated flakes. The paraffin used had a melting point of 42-45 °C. Paraffin was melted on a hot plate at 80 °C in advance. The melted paraffin was dropped onto a sample placed on a spin coater. A heat blower (hair dryer) was applied to keep the paraffin in a melted state. PL spectra were measured through the transparent paraffin film. Optical microscopy and PL mapping images were used to observe the monolayers. Raman spectra were used to analyze Eʹ and Aʹ peak positions in 30 samples of monolayer MoS 2 . The Eʹ peak represents in-plane vibrations sensitive to strain in the layer. The Aʹ peak represents out-of-plane vibrations sensitive to carrier concentration.

Key Results
MoS 2 , WS 2 , WSe 2 , and MoSe 2 showed enhancement factors of 215-, 55-, 9-, and 50-fold from the as-exfoliated flakes. For MoS 2 , a remarkable increase in PL by a factor of 215 was observed due to its low signal in the as-exfoliated state. This result suggests that paraffin film formation is widely applicable in both sulfur- and selenium-based TMDCs. These results differ from past methods such as TFSI, which is applicable only to sulfur-based TMDCs. Monolayer WS 2 showed PL enhancement of about 36 times through coating with paraffin. The normalized PL spectrum showed a decrease in the shoulder at the low-energy side. The decrease suggests a decrease in the ratio of trion-derived PL signal. The PL enhancement was observed not only on the Si/SiO 2 substrate but also on the quartz substrate. The Eʹ peak shifted in the negative direction after paraffin coating by about -0.72 cm -1 on average. The Aʹ peak shifted in the positive direction by 1.03 cm -1 after paraffin coating. The PL intensity was about 2.3 times greater in the center than at the rim of the monolayer. The PL peak position around the center shifts slightly (5-10 meV) lower in energy than the rim.
